# AI/Agent LEGO master plan — the fifteen official LEGO

**Canonical for:** the official AI/Agent LEGO set, their boundaries and their roadmap.

> These fifteen are official LEGO. They are not collapsed into one AI module, and no sixteenth top-level LEGO is created merely because a feature exists — a new feature is a sub-LEGO, a capability or an operation of an existing LEGO unless it owns a genuinely distinct lifecycle and data set.

## Canonical architecture chain

```
ai-foundation
  -> capability
  -> context-session
  -> policy
  -> skill
  -> agent-machine
  -> workspace
  -> memory
  -> artifact
  -> approval
  -> agent-event
  -> token-usage
  -> mcp-adapter
  -> runtime-adapter
  -> translation
  -> node-creator
```

AI Foundation is the FOUNDATION, not the agent loop. It owns identity, policy binding, capability resolution and provider abstraction. The agent loop belongs to Agent Machine.

`policy` in the chain is not a sixteenth LEGO. Policy binding is owned by AI Foundation and enforced at Capability and Approval; it is a responsibility, not a unit.

## Dependency graph

```
ai-foundation      -> (leaf)
skill              -> ai-foundation, capability
agent-machine      -> ai-foundation, capability, context-session, approval
memory             -> ai-foundation, storage
workspace          -> ai-foundation, capability
context-session    -> ai-foundation
translation        -> ai-foundation
node-creator       -> node-registry, capability
capability         -> (leaf)
mcp-adapter        -> ai-foundation, capability
runtime-adapter    -> ai-foundation, agent-machine
artifact           -> ai-foundation, storage
approval           -> ai-foundation, capability
agent-event        -> ai-foundation
token-usage        -> ai-foundation, context-session
```

## External action model

Every external action routes through Capability + Policy + Workspace. An agent never receives unrestricted OS authority by default.

| Capability | Side effects | Workspace-scoped | Approval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filesystem.read` | read-only | yes | — |
| `filesystem.write` | writes | yes | — |
| `filesystem.patch` | writes | yes | — |
| `terminal.execute` | destructive | yes | high-risk activity requires approval |
| `project.create` | writes | yes | — |
| `project.build` | writes | yes | — |
| `project.test` | writes | yes | — |
| `browser.open` | external | yes | — |
| `git.status` | read-only | yes | — |
| `git.diff` | read-only | yes | — |
| `git.commit` | writes | yes | — |
| `github.create_pr` | external | no | required |

**contract-only — none of these capabilities is implemented**

## 2. Skill

> Package knowledge, rules, procedure and a capability map into a selectable, progressively disclosed unit.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Index | 2 of 15 |
| Owner | `manager` |
| Status | **IMPLEMENTED** |
| Phase | B |
| Contracts | `ai.skill` |
| Versioning | ai.skill@1.0.0 |
| Depends on | `ai-foundation`, `capability` |
| Interaction | `call` |
| Permissions | `ai:skill:read`, `ai:skill:select` |
| Resource profile | `low-resource` |

**Scope:** skill registration, skill selection, progressive disclosure, capability mapping

**NOT in scope:** executing tools directly, being an agent, owning model choice, owning memory

**Lifecycle:** `registered` -> `available` -> `selected` -> `loaded` -> `active` -> `released`

**Operations:** `list`, `resolve`, `describe`, `validate-selection`

**Replacement boundary:** A skill's procedure may be rewritten without changing its identity or card.

**Degradation:** `available`, `optional-absent`

**Observability:** skill selected / loaded / released.

**Tests:** `test/lego-skill.test.mjs`

**Future stages:** D: authoring · E: skill packs

**Definition:** Skill = knowledge + rules + procedure + capability map.

**Progressive disclosure:**

- `L0` — identity — id, title, one line. Always cheap to list.
- `L1` — card — when to use it, what it needs, what it produces.
- `L2` — procedure — the steps.
- `L3` — deep knowledge — references, examples, edge cases.

> A skill is selected on L0/L1 and only then loaded deeper. Loading every skill's L3 into context is how a context window is exhausted before any work starts.

## 4. Memory

> Own persistent knowledge as a traversable graph — not the current context window.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Index | 4 of 15 |
| Owner | `manager` |
| Status | **IMPLEMENTED** |
| Phase | B |
| Contracts | `ai.memory` |
| Versioning | ai.memory@1.0.0 |
| Depends on | `ai-foundation`, `storage` |
| Interaction | `call`, `batch` |
| Permissions | `ai:memory:read`, `ai:memory:write` |
| Resource profile | `standard` |

**Scope:** memory graph, retention classes, relevance traversal, memory providers

**NOT in scope:** being the context window, being the session, dumping full memory into a prompt

**Lifecycle:** `declared` -> `available` -> `active` -> `degraded` -> `disabled`

**Operations:** `memory.remember`, `memory.recall`, `memory.list`, `memory.forget`

**Replacement boundary:** Graph storage may move from local JSON to SQLite to a graph store behind the same contract.

**Degradation:** `available`, `degraded`, `optional-absent`

**Observability:** memory read/write counts; never content.

**Tests:** `test/lego-memory.test.mjs (create, recall, empty, invalid, duplicate, update, isolation, provider, integrity, forget, ordering, limits)`

**Future stages:** traverse: relevance-ranked graph traversal · relate: explicit edge creation as first-class operation · retention enforcement: policy-driven archival · provider adapters: SQLite, filesystem snapshot, Obsidian projection as adapters

**Distinction:** Memory is persistent knowledge. Context is what is loaded right now. Conflating them produces a system that either forgets everything or loads everything.

**Memory graph:**

- Nodes: `project`, `workflow`, `node`, `execution`, `agent`, `session`, `decision`, `evidence`, `artifact`, `task`
- Edges: `depends_on`, `caused`, `derived_from`, `supports`, `contradicts`, `implements`, `belongs_to`, `delegated_to`, `decided_by`, `observed_in`, `related_to`

**Retention classes:** `EPHEMERAL` < `WORKING` < `IMPORTANT` < `DURABLE` < `PERMANENT`

> Never dump full memory into context. Load by graph traversal plus relevance, bounded by the caller's budget.

> Obsidian is a Memory Provider / human knowledge interface adapter. It is NOT the internal source of truth, and the memory graph must remain valid with no provider connected.

| Resource profile | `low-resource` |

**Scope:** context scopes, session identity, usage monitoring, threshold detection, compaction, continuation package, session rollover, rehydration, verification

**NOT in scope:** being persistent memory, storing transcripts inside session state

**Lifecycle:** `declared` -> `active` -> `prepare` -> `compacting` -> `rolled-over` -> `closed`

**Operations:** `load`, `compact`, `rollover`, `rehydrate`, `verify`

**Replacement boundary:** Compaction strategy is swappable behind the contract.

**Degradation:** `available`, `degraded`, `migration-required`

**Observability:** context.loaded, context.compacted.

**Distinction:** Conversation != Session != Context Window != Memory != Execution. One conversation may contain many sessions and many context windows.

**Scopes:** `GLOBAL` > `WORKFLOW` > `NODE` > `EXECUTION` > `EVENT` > `AGENT` > `TASK`

**Continuation package:** `identity`, `objective`, `plan`, `completedWork`, `unfinishedWork`, `constraints`, `decisions`, `activeEntities`, `toolStateReferences`, `artifacts`, `importantReferences`, `errors`, `unresolvedQuestions`, `compressedHistory`

> Never wait for the exact context limit. Rollover is triggered at a declared threshold, because a rollover attempted at 100% has no room left to write the continuation package — the one operation that makes the rollover survivable.

## 13. Approval

> Be the formal control boundary for consequential actions.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Index | 13 of 15 |
| Owner | `manager` |
| Status | **CONTRACT-ONLY** |
| Phase | C |
| Contracts | `ai.approval` |
| Versioning | ai.approval@1.0.0 |
| Depends on | `ai-foundation`, `capability` |
| Interaction | `call`, `event` |
| Permissions | `ai:approval:request`, `ai:approval:resolve`, `ai:approval:read` |
| Resource profile | `low-resource` |

**Scope:** approval request, resolution, risk classification, fail-closed policy

**NOT in scope:** approval UI, being an audit log, deciding policy for a domain it does not own

**Lifecycle:** `declared` -> `requested` -> `pending` -> `granted` -> `denied` -> `expired`

**Operations:** `request`, `resolve`, `inspect`

**Replacement boundary:** Policy engine swappable behind the contract.

**Degradation:** `available`, `permission-denied`, `capability-unavailable`

**Observability:** approval.requested / granted / denied.

**Tests:** `test/lego-ai-foundation.test.mjs (fail-closed proven)`

**Future stages:** C: store + policy · D: UI surface (agent-1)

> Child agents never inherit authority automatically.

**Requires approval:** `workflow execution`, `credential changes`, `system settings`, `resource deletion`, `git push`, `merge`, `external message`, `high-risk terminal activity`

> Unknown and destructive actions FAIL CLOSED. An expired or unanswered approval is a DENY. Read-only must be proven, never assumed — the tempting `list.includes(action)` implementation returns false for anything new, so a newly added destructive action would need no approval until someone remembered to extend the list.

**Event fields:** `timestamp`, `sessionId`, `agentId`, `parentId`, `taskId`, `type`, `status`, `duration`, `summary`, `refs` (26 types)

> Work Trace represents operational activity, NOT private reasoning. Chain-of-thought is never stored: it is not an audit format, and retaining it creates a liability with no operational benefit.

## 15. Token & Usage

> Account for token and resource usage honestly, distinguishing reported from estimated.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Index | 15 of 15 |
| Owner | `manager` |
| Status | **IN-PROGRESS** |
| Phase | D |
| Contracts | `ai.token-usage` |
| Versioning | ai.token-usage@1.0.0 |
| Depends on | `ai-foundation`, `context-session` |
| Interaction | `call`, `event` |
| Permissions | `ai:usage:read`, `ai:usage:write` |
| Resource profile | `low-resource` |

**Scope:** message tokens, model input tokens, output tokens, total tokens, budget, resource accounting, context rollover input, session statistics, agent usage, provider usage

**NOT in scope:** fabricating provider metrics, billing, owning the UI

**Lifecycle:** `declared` -> `accounting` -> `active` -> `degraded` -> `optional-absent`

**Operations:** `record`, `query`, `budget`

**Replacement boundary:** Accounting backend swappable.

**Degradation:** `available`, `degraded`, `optional-absent`

**Observability:** usage per session/agent/provider.

**Tests:** `test/lego-token-usage.test.mjs (record provenance, zero-vs-unavailable, estimator identity, idempotent requestId, budget derivation, cost pricing basis, secret/content refusal)`, `planned: UI surface (agent-1), provider-reported metrics (stage E)`

**Future stages:** D: accounting · D: UI surface (agent-1) · E: provider-reported metrics

**Sources:** `reported` vs `estimated`

> Never fabricate provider metrics. A token count that the provider did not report is `estimated` and must be labelled as such — an estimate presented as a measurement is worse than no number, because it cannot be audited.

**UI rule:** Message text stays dominant; per-message token metadata stays subtle (e.g. `· 8 tokens`). A detailed view may expose message/context/output/total/source. Context-level usage may show e.g. `Context 61%`. (agent-1 owns the rendering; this LEGO owns the numbers and their provenance.)
